title: Peace on the Messengers; Pride of the Disbelievers

paragraphs.text: When the punishment comes down into the territory of the disbelievers, the morning of those who were warned will be very bad. So the Prophet is told again to leave them for a while and watch, for they will see. Your Lord, the Lord of might, is exalted above what they say about Him. Peace be upon the messengers, and all praise belongs to Allah, Lord of the worlds.

Surah Sad begins with an oath by the Qur'an, which contains a reminder. Yet the disbelievers are full of pride and are against the truth. Allah destroyed many generations before them, and those people cried out for help, but it was no longer a time to escape. The disbelievers are surprised that a warner has come from among themselves, and they call him a magician and a liar. They ask in amazement whether he has turned all their gods into only one, calling this a very strange thing. Their leaders went out telling the people to continue and to stay patient in defending their gods, saying that this was something intended. They said they had never heard of this in the latest religion and that it was only a made-up story. They asked why the message had been sent down to him alone out of all of them. In truth, they are in doubt about Allah's message, because they have not yet tasted His punishment.

Do they own the treasures of the mercy of the Lord, the Mighty, the Giver? Or do they rule the heavens, the earth and what is between them? If so, they should climb up by any way they can. In fact, they are only an army that will be defeated there, among the other groups who opposed the truth.

great wealth that is kept safe
